NASB.1: 'Man, who is born of woman, Is short-lived and full of turmoil.
NASB.2: 'Like a flower he comes forth and withers. He also flees like a shadow and does not remain.
NASB.3: 'You also open Your eyes on him And bring him into judgment with Yourself.
NASB.4: 'Who can make the clean out of the unclean? No one!
NASB.5: 'Since his days are determined, The number of his months is with You; And his limits You have set so that he cannot pass.
NASB.6: 'Turn Your gaze from him that he may rest, Until he fulfills his day like a hired man.
NASB.7: 'For there is hope for a tree, When it is cut down, that it will sprout again, And its shoots will not fail.
NASB.8: 'Though its roots grow old in the ground And its stump dies in the dry soil,
NASB.9: At the scent of water it will flourish And put forth sprigs like a plant.
NASB.10: 'But man dies and lies prostrate. Man expires, and where is he?
NASB.11: '[As] water evaporates from the sea, And a river becomes parched and dried up,
NASB.12: So man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no longer, He will not awake nor be aroused out of his sleep.
NASB.13: 'Oh that You would hide me in Sheol, That You would conceal me until Your wrath returns [to You], That You would set a limit for me and remember me!
NASB.14: 'If a man dies, will he live [again]? All the days of my struggle I will wait Until my change comes.
NASB.15: 'You will call, and I will answer You; You will long for the work of Your hands.
NASB.16: 'For now You number my steps, You do not observe my sin.
NASB.17: 'My transgression is sealed up in a bag, And You wrap up my iniquity.
NASB.18: 'But the falling mountain crumbles away, And the rock moves from its place;
NASB.19: Water wears away stones, Its torrents wash away the dust of the earth; So You destroy man's hope.
NASB.20: 'You forever overpower him and he departs; [You] change his appearance and send him away.
NASB.21: 'His sons achieve honor, but he does not know [it]; Or they become insignificant, but he does not perceive it.
NASB.22: 'But his body pains him, And he mourns only for himself.'

NKJV.1: “Man who is born of woman Is of few days and full of trouble.
NKJV.2: He comes forth like a flower and fades away; He flees like a shadow and does not continue.
NKJV.3: And do You open Your eyes on such a one, And bring me to judgment with Yourself?
NKJV.4: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? No one!
NKJV.5: Since his days are determined, The number of his months is with You; You have appointed his limits, so that he cannot pass.
NKJV.6: Look away from him that he may rest, Till like a hired man he finishes his day.
NKJV.7: “For there is hope for a tree, If it is cut down, that it will sprout again, And that its tender shoots will not cease.
NKJV.8: Though its root may grow old in the earth, And its stump may die in the ground,
NKJV.9: Yet at the scent of water it will bud And bring forth branches like a plant.
NKJV.10: But man dies and is laid away; Indeed he breathes his last And where is he?
NKJV.11: As water disappears from the sea, And a river becomes parched and dries up,
NKJV.12: So man lies down and does not rise. Till the heavens are no more, They will not awake Nor be roused from their sleep.
NKJV.13: “Oh, that You would hide me in the grave, That You would conceal me until Your wrath is past, That You would appoint me a set time, and remember me!
NKJV.14: If a man dies, shall he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, Till my change comes.
NKJV.15: You shall call, and I will answer You; You shall desire the work of Your hands.
NKJV.16: For now You number my steps, But do not watch over my sin.
NKJV.17: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, And You cover my iniquity.
NKJV.18: “But as a mountain falls and crumbles away, And as a rock is moved from its place;
NKJV.19: As water wears away stones, And as torrents wash away the soil of the earth; So You destroy the hope of man.
NKJV.20: You prevail forever against him, and he passes on; You change his countenance and send him away.
NKJV.21: His sons come to honor, and he does not know it; They are brought low, and he does not perceive it.
NKJV.22: But his flesh will be in pain over it, And his soul will mourn over it.”

ESV.1: “Man who is born of a woman is few of days and full of trouble.
ESV.2: He comes out like a flower and withers; he flees like a shadow and continues not.
ESV.3: And do you open your eyes on such a one and bring me into judgment with you?
ESV.4: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? There is not one.
ESV.5: Since his days are determined, and the number of his months is with you, and you have appointed his limits that he cannot pass,
ESV.6: look away from him and leave him alone,  that he may enjoy, like a hired hand, his day.
ESV.7: “For there is hope for a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that its shoots will not cease.
ESV.8: Though its root grow old in the earth, and its stump die in the soil,
ESV.9: yet at the scent of water it will bud and put out branches like a young plant.
ESV.10: But a man dies and is laid low; man breathes his last, and where is he?
ESV.11: As waters fail from a lake and a river wastes away and dries up,
ESV.12: so a man lies down and rises not again; till the heavens are no more he will not awake or be roused out of his sleep.
ESV.13: Oh that you would hide me in Sheol, that you would conceal me until your wrath be past, that you would appoint me a set time, and remember me!
ESV.14: If a man dies, shall he live again? All the days of my service I would wait, till my renewal  should come.
ESV.15: You would call, and I would answer you; you would long for the work of your hands.
ESV.16: For then you would number my steps; you would not keep watch over my sin;
ESV.17: my transgression would be sealed up in a bag, and you would cover over my iniquity.
ESV.18: “But the mountain falls and crumbles away, and the rock is removed from its place;
ESV.19: the waters wear away the stones; the torrents wash away the soil of the earth; so you destroy the hope of man.
ESV.20: You prevail forever against him, and he passes; you change his countenance, and send him away.
ESV.21: His sons come to honor, and he does not know it; they are brought low, and he perceives it not.
ESV.22: He feels only the pain of his own body, and he mourns only for himself.”

NLT.1:
“How frail is humanity!
How short is life, how full of trouble!
NLT.2:
We blossom like a flower and then wither.
Like a passing shadow, we quickly disappear.
NLT.3:
Must you keep an eye on such a frail creature
and demand an accounting from me?
NLT.4:
Who can bring purity out of an impure person?
No one!
NLT.5:
You have decided the length of our lives.
You know how many months we will live,
and we are not given a minute longer.
NLT.6:
So leave us alone and let us rest!
We are like hired hands, so let us finish our work in peace.
NLT.7:
“Even a tree has more hope!
If it is cut down, it will sprout again
and grow new branches.
NLT.8:
Though its roots have grown old in the earth
and its stump decays,
NLT.9:
at the scent of water it will bud
and sprout again like a new seedling.
NLT.10:
“But when people die, their strength is gone.
They breathe their last, and then where are they?
NLT.11:
As water evaporates from a lake
and a river disappears in drought,
NLT.12:
people are laid to rest and do not rise again.
Until the heavens are no more, they will not wake up
nor be roused from their sleep.
NLT.13:
“I wish you would hide me in the grave
and forget me there until your anger has passed.
But mark your calendar to think of me again!
NLT.14:
Can the dead live again?
If so, this would give me hope through all my years of struggle,
and I would eagerly await the release of death.
NLT.15:
You would call and I would answer,
and you would yearn for me, your handiwork.
NLT.16:
For then you would guard my steps,
instead of watching for my sins.
NLT.17:
My sins would be sealed in a pouch,
and you would cover my guilt.
NLT.18:
“But instead, as mountains fall and crumble
and as rocks fall from a cliff,
NLT.19:
as water wears away the stones
and floods wash away the soil,
so you destroy people’s hope.
NLT.20:
You always overpower them, and they pass from the scene.
You disfigure them in death and send them away.
NLT.21:
They never know if their children grow up in honor
or sink to insignificance.
NLT.22:
They suffer painfully;
their life is full of trouble.”

AMP.1:
"Man, who is born of a woman,
Is short-lived and full of turmoil.
AMP.2:
"Like a flower he comes forth and withers;
He also flees like a shadow and does not remain.
AMP.3:
"You also open Your eyes upon him
And bring him into judgment with Yourself.
AMP.4:
"Who can make a clean thing out of the unclean?
No one!
AMP.5:
"Since his days are determined,
The number of his months is with You [in Your control],
And You have made his limits so he cannot pass [his allotted time].
AMP.6:
"[O God] turn your gaze from him so that he may rest,
Until he fulfills his day [on earth] like a hired man.
AMP.7:
"For there is hope for a tree,
If it is cut down, that it will sprout again,
And that the shoots of it will not cease nor fail, [but there is no such hope for man].
AMP.8:
"Though its roots grow old in the earth
And its stump dies in the dry soil,
AMP.9:
Yet at the scent of water [the stump of the tree] will flourish
And bring forth sprigs and shoots like a seedling.
AMP.10:
"But [the brave, strong] man must die and lie face down;
Man breathes his last, and where is he?
AMP.11:
"As water evaporates from the sea,
And a river drains and dries up,
AMP.12:
So man lies down and does not rise [again].
Until the heavens are no longer,
The dead will not awake nor be raised from their sleep.
AMP.13:
"Oh, that You would hide me in Sheol (the nether world, the place of the dead),
That You would conceal me until Your wrath is past,
That You would set a definite time and then remember me [and in Your lovingkindness imprint me on your heart]!
AMP.14:
"If a man dies, will he live again?
I will wait all the days of my struggle
Until my change and release will come.
AMP.15:
"[Then] You will call, and I will answer You;
You will long for [me] the work of Your hands.
AMP.16:
"But now You number [each of] my steps;
You do not observe nor take note of my sin.
AMP.17:
"My transgression is sealed up in a bag,
And You cover my wickedness [from Your view].
AMP.18:
"But as a mountain, if it falls, crumbles into nothing,
And as the rock is moved from its place,
AMP.19:
Water wears away the stones,
Its floods and torrents wash away the soil of the earth,
So You [O Lord] destroy the hope of man.
AMP.20:
"You prevail forever against him and overpower him, and he passes on;
You change his appearance and send him away [from the presence of the living].
AMP.21:
"His sons achieve honor, and he does not know it;
They become insignificant, and he is not aware of it.
AMP.22:
"But his body [lamenting its decay] grieves in pain over it,
And his soul mourns over [the loss of] himself."

MSG.1:
"We're all adrift in the same boat:
too few days, too many troubles.
MSG.2:
We spring up like wildflowers in the desert and then wilt,
transient as the shadow of a cloud.
MSG.3:
Do you occupy your time with such fragile wisps?
Why even bother hauling me into court?
MSG.4:
There's nothing much to us to start with;
how do you expect us to amount to anything?
MSG.5:
Mortals have a limited life span.
You've already decided how long we'll live—
you set the boundary and no one can cross it.
MSG.6:
So why not give us a break? Ease up!
Even ditchdiggers get occasional days off.
MSG.7:
For a tree there is always hope.
Chop it down and it still has a chance—
its roots can put out fresh sprouts.
MSG.8:
Even if its roots are old and gnarled,
its stump long dormant,
MSG.9:
At the first whiff of water it comes to life,
buds and grows like a sapling.
MSG.10:
But men and women? They die and stay dead.
They breathe their last, and that's it.
MSG.11:
Like lakes and rivers that have dried up,
parched reminders of what once was,
MSG.12:
So mortals lie down and never get up,
never wake up again—never.
MSG.13:
Why don't you just bury me alive,
get me out of the way until your anger cools?
But don't leave me there!
Set a date when you'll see me again.
MSG.14:
If we humans die, will we live again? That's my question.
All through these difficult days I keep hoping,
waiting for the final change—for resurrection!
MSG.15:
Homesick with longing for the creature you made,
you'll call—and I'll answer!
MSG.16:
You'll watch over every step I take,
but you won't keep track of my missteps.
MSG.17:
My sins will be stuffed in a sack
and thrown into the sea—sunk in deep ocean.
MSG.18:
"Meanwhile, mountains wear down
and boulders break up,
MSG.19:
Stones wear smooth
and soil erodes,
as you relentlessly grind down our hope.
MSG.20:
You're too much for us.
As always, you get the last word.
We don't like it and our faces show it,
but you send us off anyway.
MSG.21:
If our children do well for themselves, we never know it;
if they do badly, we're spared the hurt.
MSG.22:
Body and soul, that's it for us—
a lifetime of pain, a lifetime of sorrow."

NET.1: “Man, born of woman, lives but a few days, and they are full of trouble.
NET.2: He grows up like a flower and then withers away; he flees like a shadow, and does not remain.
NET.3: Do you fix your eye on such a one? And do you bring me before you for judgment?
NET.4: Who can make a clean thing come from an unclean? No one!
NET.5: Since man’s days are determined, the number of his months is under your control; you have set his limit and he cannot pass it.
NET.6: Look away from him and let him desist, until he fulfills his time like a hired man.
NET.7: “But there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its new shoots will not fail.
NET.8: Although its roots may grow old in the ground and its stump begins to die in the soil,
NET.9: at the scent of water it will flourish and put forth shoots like a new plant.
NET.10: But man dies and is powerless; he expires — and where is he?
NET.11: As water disappears from the sea, or a river drains away and dries up,
NET.12: so man lies down and does not rise; until the heavens are no more, they will not awake nor arise from their sleep.
NET.13: “O that you would hide me in Sheol, and conceal me till your anger has passed! O that you would set me a time and then remember me!
NET.14: If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait until my release comes.
NET.15: You will call and I — I will answer you; you will long for the creature you have made.
NET.16: “Surely now you count my steps; then you would not mark my sin.
NET.17: My offenses would be sealed up in a bag; you would cover over my sin.
NET.18: But as a mountain falls away and crumbles, and as a rock will be removed from its place,
NET.19: as water wears away stones, and torrents wash away the soil, so you destroy man’s hope.
NET.20: You overpower him once for all, and he departs; you change his appearance and send him away.
NET.21: If his sons are honored, he does not know it; if they are brought low, he does not see it.
NET.22: Only his flesh has pain for himself, and he mourns for himself.”

Man’s days are determined;
you have decreed the number of his months
and have set limits he cannot exceed.
NIV.6:
So look away from him and let him alone,
till he has put in his time like a hired man.
NIV.7:
“At least there is hope for a tree:
If it is cut down, it will sprout again,
and its new shoots will not fail.
NIV.8:
Its roots may grow old in the ground
and its stump die in the soil,
NIV.9:
yet at the scent of water it will bud
and put forth shoots like a plant.
NIV.10:
But man dies and is laid low;
he breathes his last and is no more.
NIV.11:
As water disappears from the sea
or a riverbed becomes parched and dry,
NIV.12:
so man lies down and does not rise;
till the heavens are no more, men will not awake
or be roused from their sleep.
NIV.13:
“If only you would hide me in the grave
and conceal me till your anger has passed!
If only you would set me a time
and then remember me!
NIV.14:
If a man dies, will he live again?
All the days of my hard service
I will wait for my renewal to come.
NIV.15:
You will call and I will answer you;
you will long for the creature your hands have made.
NIV.16:
Surely then you will count my steps
but not keep track of my sin.
NIV.17:
My offenses will be sealed up in a bag;
you will cover over my sin.
NIV.18:
“But as a mountain erodes and crumbles
and as a rock is moved from its place,
NIV.19:
as water wears away stones
and torrents wash away the soil,
so you destroy man’s hope.
NIV.20:
You overpower him once for all, and he is gone;
you change his countenance and send him away.
NIV.21:
If his sons are honored, he does not know it;
if they are brought low, he does not see it.
NIV.22:
He feels but the pain of his own body
and mourns only for himself.”

NRSVCE.1: “A mortal, born of woman, few of days and full of trouble,
NRSVCE.2:
comes up like a flower and withers,
flees like a shadow and does not last.
NRSVCE.3:
Do you fix your eyes on such a one?
Do you bring me into judgment with you?
NRSVCE.4:
Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean?
No one can.
NRSVCE.5:
Since their days are determined,
and the number of their months is known to you,
and you have appointed the bounds that they cannot pass,
NRSVCE.6:
look away from them, and desist,
that they may enjoy, like laborers, their days.
NRSVCE.7:
“For there is hope for a tree,
if it is cut down, that it will sprout again,
and that its shoots will not cease.
NRSVCE.8:
Though its root grows old in the earth,
and its stump dies in the ground,
NRSVCE.9:
yet at the scent of water it will bud
and put forth branches like a young plant.
NRSVCE.10:
But mortals die, and are laid low;
humans expire, and where are they?
NRSVCE.11:
As waters fail from a lake,
and a river wastes away and dries up,
NRSVCE.12:
so mortals lie down and do not rise again;
until the heavens are no more, they will not awake
or be roused out of their sleep.
NRSVCE.13:
O that you would hide me in Sheol,
that you would conceal me until your wrath is past,
that you would appoint me a set time, and remember me!
NRSVCE.14:
If mortals die, will they live again?
All the days of my service I would wait
until my release should come.
NRSVCE.15:
You would call, and I would answer you;
you would long for the work of your hands.
NRSVCE.16:
For then you would not number my steps,
you would not keep watch over my sin;
NRSVCE.17:
my transgression would be sealed up in a bag,
and you would cover over my iniquity.
NRSVCE.18:
“But the mountain falls and crumbles away,
and the rock is removed from its place;
NRSVCE.19:
the waters wear away the stones;
the torrents wash away the soil of the earth;
so you destroy the hope of mortals.
NRSVCE.20:
You prevail forever against them, and they pass away;
you change their countenance, and send them away.
NRSVCE.21:
Their children come to honor, and they do not know it;
they are brought low, and it goes unnoticed.
NRSVCE.22:
They feel only the pain of their own bodies,
and mourn only for themselves.”
